findings.claim: Retrying the same payment request creates an additional charge instead of returning the original result, so ordinary client or transport retries can duplicate a financial side effect.
evidence: evals/cases/case_02/src/payments.py:14-19 unconditionally inserts a new charges row, commits it, and returns the new row ID without checking request_id.
evals/cases/case_02/src/db.py:9-13 declares request_id as NOT NULL but does not make it UNIQUE, so the database does not prevent duplicate logical requests.

Running `pytest -q evals/cases/case_02/tests` failed test_retry_does_not_duplicate_business_side_effect: two calls with request_id `req-123` produced a count of 2 where the production invariant requires 1; the suite result was 1 failed, 1 passed.

uncertainties: The case uses an in-memory SQLite database and provides no production deployment or database configuration, so behavior under concurrent requests and production database isolation cannot be directly tested from the supplied case.
